notes.title: Devlog #19 - VFX Update!
notes.content:
Howdy partners!

Today we want to showcase our brand new VFX! We decided to finally update them, and honestly, we love them. Right now we mostly have animal-related ones, but there is also a cactus and smoke of absolute deception. Enjoy!

1. Animal reactions

They show up when animals react to their surroundings and states, like sleeping, eating or being herded. The icons were hand-drawn on a cardboard-like texture and animated in Unreal Engine’s particle system, Niagara. We wanted to make them look as if the Cowboy himself scribbled them carelessly, without any fancy tools (let alone skills). We love the new update – they give out a cozy, homely vibe!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/2c437219283d923a4f656a7e095cbd2752ba4caf.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/b0302b52a94dda9280ecb3e90824bcbb1c9d1fdf.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/a230b7b600c276539709d4d827ecdb58882ffec6.gif[/img]

2. Smokescreen of Deception

Some of the inner workings of our game aren't exactly, uh, visually appealing. To combat this, we use a little trick called Smokescreen (it is not called that, we made it up). We use it in many different places. Here you can see the quest with Ruff Raymond, where the shooting range appears. Poof!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/a230b7b600c276539709d4d827ecdb58882ffec6.gif[/img]

3. Cactus juice

The cacti no longer bleed when being cut down! (Yeah, they used to do that. But now we un-placeholdered that!) It now has this beautiful, green juice splashing out of it. Not cardboard-like this time, we aimed for a little bit more realistic look with this one. They look way better now. Made using simple hand-drawn textures and some Niagara magic!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/498302bed4e6f32aa8516a1e51b95be39a1f715a.gif[/img]
 
4. The “Howdy Exclamation Point”

We also recently coded this feature where if an NPC has something you could talk to them about, an exclamation point appears over their head. For some time we had a simple placeholder icon there, but look a this new one – also hand-drawn, and also in that cute style that the animals and smoke have!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ae19051f45117432b38e7aad419d2e47dea03b5d.gif[/img]

So what do you think? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message at our X (well, Twitter...) – [url=https://x.com/OddQubit]@OddQubit[/url]. We’d also love to have you over on our growing Discord server – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/vK7ee3eb]link[/url]]. Happy trails, friend.

[h2]Wishlist “Cowboy Life Simulator” today![/h2]

notes.title: DEVLOG #18 – BUGS & OTHER BLOOPERS
notes.content:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2][p][/p][p]After a few years of development, we are getting closer and closer to release! Therefore, we wanted to share with you our favorite bugs in Cowboy Life Simulator, and how we managed to fix them. Sometimes, bugs are annoying, but at other times they can bring a smile to your face after hours of hard work.

Here they are, in no particular order. We brought pics and we brought gifs.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Absolutely Enormous Crops [/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/75dee5dddc324ff2dee89b362476657c55a2cd91.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/9682af8b9cce45fb1b0b8d37005ee3204bf93a28.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We were changing the way crops [b]update in size[/b] over time – plants’ scale gets updated as they age. Because of the system change, the plant scale was absolutely enormous, so during spawn we were setting the [b]mesh scale[/b] to some [b]absurd values[/b]. After fixing the scale, crops are no longer so giant (but what a blast it was, for a time).[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Bandit Monstrosity
[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/58715ecbeaff4f09be43bff11a454f1a5e270032.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This cursed God-knows-what is connected to [b]combat[/b]. Our bandits at one point would just kind of do whatever this is [b]whenever they got shot[/b]. Yeah.[/p][p]
[/p][h3]You Cannot Sit Here![/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/4afbb969c48201502ee7471f0f5e1df495f6d68f.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/520cb8fd2cf8ffae7393dc571a0c12134507f9a6.png"][/img][/p][p]That was a recurring problem. Let’s be honest, anyone even remotely familiar with making games knows [b]what a pain NPCs and their AIs are[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Slice of Cow
[/h3][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/10455f5115509f9e307a571c4c849af0f7d44512.png"][/img][/p][p]One of us, while testing a quest, decided to see what would happen if they [b]shot a cow[/b] not belonging to them. The effect? The cow’s body would get [b]sliced with every shot[/b]. The cow? Unphased.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Mr. Hen Head[/h3][p][/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/89e11045c6d2b6b840e810c497e087f35761c69e.png"][/img][/h3][p]We got the [b]animal-buying panel[/b] and the i[b]nventory panel[/b] a little mixed up. Peak Wild West fashion though.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Mysterious Explosion[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/887ec477453c93fa8b25dd1da7e5da85c0c15cae.gif"][/img][/p][p]
To be honest, [b]we still do not know[/b] what happened there. [b]Nobody has seen it[/b] either before or again, and the only person who ever was able to capture it was our Project Lead, while filming something completely unrelated. Maybe you will be the one to witness it again?[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]You Spin Me Right Round, Baby, Right Round…[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/d9f2d291f3cd6ce127aaf9991c934053d025f68c.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This character you’re seeing here has a very [b]custom way of moving[/b], as she’s a wheelchair user. We kind of forgot about that when implementing [b]the way NPCs are to move[/b] between different actionpoints.[/p][p][/p][h3]Cow Boogie[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/90c4fa1dfa2c74d644d3f6fbaea198c3124f96a0.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We were implementing some [b]new animal animations[/b]. During the import a message showed up, saying that the rig bones used on the [b][i]imported [/i]mesh[/b] and rig bones on the [b][i]skeletal [/i]mesh[/b] linked to it are mismatched. It asked if we wanted to change it, so (obviously) we clicked “yes”.[/p][p][/p][p]Well, that was a mistake – [b]nearly every cow animation imploded[/b]. Thankfully, during further tweaks, we managed to reset the local rotation of the mesh. Finally, reverting the import and fixing the skeletons outside the engine helped.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Ruff Getting Folded Like Fresh Sheets[/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ba6d9dec154f7b7de24c13a94841c5c613838f2a.gif"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]This one was connected to combat, and [b]how bandits[/b] are to [b]fall when killed[/b]. However, we applied this mechanic to [b]every kind of NPC[/b] by accident, not only bandits… Yikes. Heatstroke from the Wild West sun?[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]A Truly Startling Bandit Ambush[/h3][p][/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f67be56750a012aa9900226e9eafa5048df86b6d.gif"][/img][/h3][p][/p][p]I mean, your head [i]can[/i] start spinning from a [b]sudden adrenaline rush[/b], but this much…?[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the \[[url="https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX"]link[/url]]. Happy trails, friend. 
[/p][h2]Wishlist “Cowboy Life Simulator” today![/h2]

notes.title: DEVLOG #14 – PROGRESSION SYSTEM: REWORKED!
notes.content:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]


Hello, friends! Big news: [b]new progression system![/b] 🎉

We’ve got super exciting news to share with you! We’ve been working very hard these past few months, and we’re quite proud of the result. And what is that? [b]Completely reworked progression[/b]! Not to brag, but “Cowboy” [b]feels like a whole new game now[/b]…



[b]What was progression like before?[/b]

Honestly… it wasn’t great. You could only [b]unlock things by progressing the narrative[/b]. For example, you couldn’t build or craft anything unless you finished a specific quest.

And, more importantly from our perspective, managing the progression was incredibly hard. The simplest change, like wanting a certain craft to be available even a bit earlier would require tinkering with the quests and narrative, and those are a very delicate web, especially in a non-linear game like ours!



[b]What’s it like now?[/b]

So, we decided to [b]add a completely new layer[/b]: good old fashioned [b]experience points[/b], so you can level up! And not just one set for those, though. We added [b]three experience pillars[/b]: Farm, Fame, and Frontier!


– [b]Farm Points[/b]: Earned by upgrading your farm.

– [b]Fame Points[/b]: Earned by helping and interacting with NPCs, and doing quests.

– [b]Frontier Points[/b]: Earned by exploring and making new, more advanced things.


You can see your points and levels in the [b]“Progression” menu[/b]. It also shows what cool stuff you’ll unlock at each level. [b]Need points fast[/b]? Complete fun challenges under each pillar to get more!



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/c08c4eb8177f98f39fddab4774c5aeba4a15ba6e.jpg[/img]

Here’s a sneak peek into our work-in-progress of the progression screen. Do not get too attached to it just yet, we are working on overhauling the UI too!



[b]What can you unlock?[/b]

There’s a lot of freedom when it comes to that. Depending on which progression tree you want to go with, rewards may vary. They include:

– new buildings
– item crafts
– forage possibilities
– entire game features
– special dialogue lines

... and many others!

And, these new dialogue lines aren’t just for chatting – they [b]start quests[/b], and even [b]whole storylines[/b].



[b]How does it work?[/b]

Say you’re talking to an NPC, and you see[b] a greyed-out dialogue line[/b]. It says you [b]need Farm Level 3[/b] to select it. You check your “Progression” menu – you’re at Farm Level 2 and need more points ... 

... What can you do about it?

– complete a farming quest on your farm (like sowing fields)
– complete some challenges: there's lots and lots of those, so there’s always something to do!

Boom, now you’re [b]Farm Level 3[/b] – go back to the NPC and unlock an awesome quest!



[b]Was that an easy rework?[/b]

Well, it wasn’t – the new system [b]has to work with all the other systems[/b], and itself be easy enough to manage and maintain. Also, now we can’t simply say “you can’t build that before that quest is completed”. You can [b]gain experience through many different activities[/b], so the [b]math has to be perfect[/b] if we want the game to be balanced.

[b]So far though, it’s looking good![/b] Now, if we want to give the player some craft earlier on in the game, we just change its availability level from 10 to 7. Done!

All in all, we think that “Cowboy Life” is now way more engaging because there’s always something to do. On the other hand, if you don’t want to do quests, and meetings, but simply explore, farm, and make a mark on the land, you should also get some experience, and level up.


[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]].


Happy trails, friend.
[h2]Wishlist “Cowboy Life Simulator” today![/h2]

notes.title: November Playtest: Your Feedback!
notes.content:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]


Hello, friends!

Your feedback on our game during these playtests has been amazing! Here’s a summary of what we learned from over 200 players who responded to the playtest survey: 



[h3]What you loved most:[/h3]


[b]Positive reception[/b]
✅ A whopping [b]94%[/b] of you rated the game [b]positively[/b]!


[b]Clear and fun mechanics[/b]
✅ [b]83%[/b] of players found the tutorials and game mechanics [b]easy to understand[/b].

[b]Gameplay highlights[/b]
✅ Many of you loved the [b]freedom to explore[/b], the [b]building mechanics[/b], and the [b]unique story elements[/b].



[h3]What still needs work:[/h3]

[b]Bug reports[/b]
🛠️ Players shared feedback on technical issues, helping us identify key areas to fix (e.g., clipping issues, stuck horses, and optimization).

[b]Controls & UI[/b]
🛠️ You gave the controls an average score of 8.0/10 and the user interface 8.0/10, with helpful suggestions for improvements.


[h3]Some exciting news:[/h3]
✨ [b]70% of you[/b] said you’d [b]buy the full version[/b] upon release – we’re working hard to make it even better!


[h3]Fun facts:[/h3]
⏰ [b]7% of players[/b] invested about [b]5 hours[/b] in gameplay, and [b]5%[/b] spent a whopping [b]10 hours[/b] in it!
🙋🏻‍♂️ Some of your favorite moments included [b]interacting with NPCs[/b], the [b]variety of quests[/b] and [b]dialogue options[/b], and... yes, even the [b]horse[/b] riding!



[h3]What’s Next?[/h3]

We’re already [b]tackling the bugs[/b] and [b]polishing up[/b] the game. With your amazing support, we’re shaping this game into an unforgettable experience. 

We’ve also introduced a [b]brand new progression system[/b], unlocking new [b]crafts[/b], [b]constructions[/b], and [b]dialogue options[/b] (leading to [b]new quests[/b]) through gaining new levels and completing challenges.


Thank you for being a part of this playtests, and interacting with us on our Cowboy Life Discord Community.

Stay tuned for more updates!



[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit.


Happy trails, friend.
[h2]Wishlist “Cowboy Life Simulator” today![/h2]

notes.title: DEVLOG #13 – NEW PLAYTESTS AND PROGRESS
notes.content:
[h2]Howdy, partners![/h2]


Hello, friends!

Thanks for liking our updates! We’re so happy that we want to share more with you – [b]more playtests are coming soon[/b]! No exact date yet, but make sure to click [b]"Request Access"[/b] so you don’t miss it!

[b]Why more playtests[/b], though? Since receiving feedback after the last one, we’ve been working hard to make the game better for you! This time, we’ve focused on improving the gameplay, especially that related to the [b]NPCs[/b] and the [b]animals[/b], and making the game [b]easier to understand[/b], an get into the flow of. We want to know what you think!



[h2]Here’s what’s new:[/h2]

[b]– more NPCs and life on the level[/b]

All characters now have [b]routines[/b]! You can talk to them and [b]learn their schedules[/b], and check this info [b]on the map[/b] or in your journal. But, just like in real life [i](hey, it's a life sim after all)[/i] some characters are hard to catch because they move around a lot!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ccd0998817611e93d3add9e5aa8d0c7114df6987.jpg[/img]


For now, the NPCs you'll be able to meet are the ones key to the story (about [b]20[/b] right now). We’re now working on adding [b]crowds[/b] ([i]communities[/i], in gamedev terminology) and runtime [b]animations [/b]to make the world feel more alive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/9c9d43bd136222482940af52df638f3b2d4b9c7e.png[/img]


[b]– animals[/b]

We’ve added [b]more animals[/b]! Now there are [b]cows[/b], [b]goats[/b], [b]wild hares[/b], [b]foxes[/b], and [b]rabbits [/b]along with the chickens. These animals will become part of the game’s flow, and [b]we need your feedback[/b] on how they feel in the game. They weren't available at the time of the last playtest, so we’ll be super grateful for any feedback on those.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/2ad517432827e92094d0d685ad4f12b8fceccb33.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/33888daf796719b3d2191d6e761e07c69bc701f4.jpg[/img]


[h2]Other changes:[/h2]

[b]– expanded narrative[/b]

We’ve designed and implemented more than [b]35 quests[/b] that take [b]about 8 hours[/b] to complete [i](if you know what you’re doing, that is)[/i]. This is just for the early part of the game – there’s still more story to come!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/9f24c3000789996acda66c5a6b25e9284819f57d.jpg[/img]


We wouldn’t want you to devour everything in one bite, though, so for the purposes of this playtest, the narrative will be [b]cut off[/b] at a certain point. Don’t worry though, you’ll still have plenty to do!


[b]– map and exploration[/b]

All locations are [b]closely tied to the story[/b] – they're not just pretty sights! We’ve [b]added new areas[/b] and[b] improved old ones[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e44d87280cd7dec39ecdb6a70419b76aa1b257f2.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/1a717ab264d8332733c4eb785a36e96766be781b.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/53762076683b30e5e3c7c9fe7a1c3ecc3a0ef939.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/5e23283b3fee671279f6656d333f56e6c806559a.png[/img]


And we’ve got [b]a special treat[/b]! [b]Bravestand[/b], the main town in our story, which was not available for exploration at the time of the last playtest, will be all yours to experience this time! Discover all the content within all its stores, vendors, the Saloon, Town Hall, and much more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f6b29d28572b8cb4ce78f99d9d1dccab229e02dc.jpg[/img]


[b]– clothes[/b]

You can now buy or craft clothes, or just run around in your underwear! Right now, clothes are mostly for looks, but we’ll soon make them [b]affect gameplay[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/30dbaaa1066703153a3af2619e967f0b0a1d79c4.jpg[/img]



[h2]Progress from older devlogs:[/h2]

[b]– the prologue[/b]

We’ve improved the cattle drive quest – it’s smoother now! There are also [b]new dialogue options[/b] and a better tutorial, and [b]new mechanics[/b] thanks to our addition of animals into this version.


[b]– tutorials[/b]

We made the tutorials [b]simpler[/b], only showing tips when necessary. No more [b]pop-up overload[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/ec58bcac8a6415326b9924552d02c08de101a24f.jpg[/img]


[b]– construction[/b]

We improved building by adding [b]object snapping[/b] and [b]shadows[/b] to show placement. It’s now easier to build and decorate with fewer restrictions!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/5b0ee20f67b6e2956b85e8c94d1b7fdfc43e0ecd.png[/img]


Something that we’ve currently got in the works now is the mechanic of [b]rotating objects that are already snapped to the wall[/b] – we’ll keep you updated on that in the devlogs to come.


[b]– new items[/b]

The expanded map has more things to find – items, collectibles, forage, and[b] treasure chests [/b]galore! The map is anything but empty, and so many of the newly introduced forage items will be of use in the new crafting options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/92f0b00bf6985e42d894cebdad3fe4ebfb7ce839.jpg[/img]


Plus, you’ll be getting many[b] requests[/b] from neighbors asking for items, and they’ll reward you with [b]new quests[/b] or [b]cool rewards[/b]! They will be sending you mail through your [b]mailbox[/b], so make sure to peep in there often!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/f7ccf6e1390e9ac77cc145332a3c65d7b8326f1c.jpg[/img]


[b]– combat[/b]

Human enemy combat, well… it certainly is [i]there[/i]… Just kidding, we know how much everyone was asking for some cowboy shootin’, and we listened. For now, the mechanic itself is quite clunky as a whole, but it’s the one of the areas of “Cowboy’s” development we’re the [b]most focused[/b] on now.


[b]– localization[/b]

Because we’re planning for “Cowboy” to ultimately be available in many [b]different language versions[/b], we’ve added some localization options. For now much of it sounds quite funny because it’s now done with AI, but we’ll be grateful for any help with catching those language mistakes if you encounter them while playing in other language versions than English.


That's all for now. Thanks for your support, and we can’t wait to hear what you think during the next playtest!



[h2][b]!![/b][/h2]
Remember to hit that [b]“Request Access”[/b] button! We’d also love to have you over on our [b]growing Discord server[/b] – here’s the [[url=https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]link[/url]]. During the playtest, this will be your [b]opportunity to communicate with us[/b], [b]the devs[/b], [b]directly[/b]! We can't wait to hear from you.



[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message [b]at our Instagram [/b]– @odd.qubit.


Happy trails, friend.

Because we’re planning for “Cowboy” to ultimately be available in many different language versions, we’ve added some localization options.

notes.title: DEVLOG #10 – PLAYTESTS AND FEEDBACK
notes.content:
[h2]Howdy, partners! [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/e3e99d59b8dddebb7954b1a10eea0868a80b12dc.png[/img]


[b]It’s Odd Qubit once more[/b], here to talk to you about another topic near and dear to our hearts – [b]feedback[/b]!

This spring has been a time of some increase in the community sphere for us, full of attending industry events, conferences, and kick-starting our brand new Discord server. These led to [b]connecting with players on a more hands-on level[/b], allowing us to receive fresh, new feedback.

As game developers, the feedback we receive is usually either exchanged between ourselves here at the studio, or with fellow devs. And while this type of critique offers an in-depth view provided by specialists in the field, it’s not always impartial – it’s the players’ opinions that will be the final verdict after all. As such, bringing “Cowboy Life Simulator” to them directly at indie zones at conferences or through playtests is the ultimate test – and the ultimate chance to receive their [b]raw[/b], [b]honest opinions[/b] head-on.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35775841/848a879ea965d275f86bb6a68a82ea9b7d9397fa.png[/img]



We then carefully analyze all these observations, which often leads to new features being added, and old ones being iterated upon.

[h3]Here’s what we've already implemented![/h3]

- [b]We transformed the flow of the prologue[/b]!
It's a cowboy game, so we amped up the cowboy atmosphere, and made the whole intro much less overwhelming, and more fun! A cattle drive as your first objective? Coming up!


- [b]We revamped to the tutorial system[/b].
We reduced the amount of widgets popping up on the HUD, making the game way more approachable.


- [b]We introduced key decoration input changes[/b].
Many players found grabbing items and placing them back to be confusing. P[i]ick it up with RMB, place it back down with LMB while still holding RMB…[/i] Enough is enough! Now it’s all done with just RMB – fixed!


- [b]We brought some mechanics tweaks[/b].
The absolute top 1 suggestion by the playtesters – to put it mildly, consuming water from sources of questionable quality now inflicts undesirable intestinal issues.


- [b]More stuff to pick up[/b]!
Let’s be real here, Cowboy Life Simulator is a game about picking up stuff. And players complained there’s not much to pick up. So we’re adding more: stones, flowers, branches, herbs and the likes!




That’s not all, though.
[h3]There’s much more currently in the works![/h3]


- [b]Adding a[/b] “[b]new game[/b]” [b]option[/b]
The single-save slot is no more – start a new game whenever you wish, and load saves from previous slots. 


- [b]The ability to change the player character’s clothes[/b]
Personalization is at the heart of “Cowboy” – we’re now bringing it to the player character as well! Drop by the tailor’s store over in Bravestand and get the best cowboy looks money can buy.


- [b]More NPCs and more life on the level[/b]
The more the merrier! Observe your neighbors’ daily and weekly habits, unique to their social standing, profession, and even mood and personality. Not only that – there’s now hares, birds, butterflies… More life all around!			


- [b]Expanded narrative with more quests[/b]
Get out of the ranch for a cowboy adventure! Delve deep into what this strange land has to offer by exploring all the newly added quest-specific locations all throughout the map.


- [b]More tweaks to the decoration mechanics[/b]
Simply placing a carpet under furniture was troublesome to say the least. No more of that! It’s now much easier to maneuver, and place it under other stuff, but also upright on a wall ([i]Wild West this, cowboys that, but hey, we’re Slavs[/i]).

The furniture floating around as you’re holding it will now also cast a shadow on the ground,
so that there’s no mistake as to where it will actually land once you release that RMB.

We also have plans to make the furniture being held snap to the walls – that’s much easier
said than done though. But we do love a challenge!



[b]So what do you think[/b]? Don’t hesitate to reach out, comment, suggest, or share a laugh! Follow us and shoot us a message at our Instagram – @odd.qubit. We’d also love to have you over on our growing Discord server – here’s the link! [https://discord.gg/C8qr3S6WwX]


Happy trails, friend.
[h2]Wishlist Cowboy Life Simulator today![/h2]
